PUBLIC RESPONSE: A. min 2, max 4

The two cohesive blocks that drive EJR here are the 6-voter x-block {1,2,3,8,9,10} and the 4-voter y-block {4,5,6,7}.

The x-block is 6 = 10·3/5 voters, so for ℓ=3 EJR requires a voter in the block to receive ≥3 approved seats. Every voter in the block approves x1,x2,x3 and at most one private extra: 1 has y1,z3, 2 has y2, 3 has y3, 8-10 have z1. Hence 3 can be reached with only two x’s plus the private extra. With one x the best you can do is 1 x + one private extra =2 <3, so any EJR committee must contain at least two of {x1,x2,x3}. Both of those are approved by voter 1, and y1,z3 can be avoided, so 2 is attainable, e.g.

{x1,x2,z1,y2,y4}

Voter 2 then gets x1,x2,y2 =3 and voter 4 gets y4,z1 =2, so the two blocks are satisfied and voter 1 meets exactly x1,x2.

For the upper side the y-block needs two approved seats for someone in {4,5,6,7}. Their common approvals are y4,y5,y6 and they split on z1/z2, so one y from the block together with z1 is enough to give voter 4 or 5 two seats. That uses only one seat outside voter 1’s approval set, because y4,y5,y6 and z1,z2 are all outside {x1,x2,x3,y1,z3}. 

Hence we can keep four of voter 1’s five approvals and still meet the y-block with the single remaining seat, e.g. a committee that contains x1,x2,x3,y1 and z1. $w_{x}=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|=3.$

That is the $3$-cohesive requirement of $A_{6}$; $w_{x}=2$ would give $\max_{i\in A_{6}}|W\cap A_{i}|\le2$ for the $4$-subsets $\{1,2,3,8\},\{1,2,3,9\},\{1,2,3,10\}$ once the private seats $y_{2},y_{3}$ and $z_{1}$ are used to reach the $3$ for the whole $A_{6}$.  So at least the three $x$’s are forced in $W$ and therefore at least three members of $A_{1}$ are forced in $W$.

The $y$-block is $B_{4}=\{4,5,6,7\}$.  $|B_{4}|=4\ge2n/k$ and $\bigcap B_{4}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$ so $B_{4}$ is $2$-cohesive.  $Y=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$ and $Y\cap A_{1}=\varnothing$.  With $t=|W\setminus A_{1}|$ a $B$-voter can obtain at most $t$ approvals from $Y$ and $t=1$ gives $\max_{i\in B}|W\cap A_{i}|\le1$.  Hence an EJR committee needs $t\ge2$, i.e.

$|W\cap A_{1}|=5-t\le3.$

Together with $w_{x}=3$ we have $3\le|W\cap A_{1}|\le3$.  The bound is attainable:

$W^{*}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$

$|W^{*}\cap A_{1}|=3$, $V_{1}=3$, $V_{2}=V_{3}=V_{8}=V_{9}=V_{10}=3$, $V_{4}=V_{5}=V_{6}=V_{7}=2$.
The $3$-cohesive $A_{6}$ is $3$-represented by $2,3,8,9,10$, every $4$-subset of $A_{6}$ sees the three $x$’s and is $2$-represented, and the $2$-cohesive $B_{4}$ is $2$-represented by $4,5,6,7$.    =\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$.  $B_{4}$ is $2$-cohesive and

   $Y\cap A_{1}=\varnothing$.

$|W\cap A_{i}|=w_{x}+{\bf1}_{\mathrm{priv}(i)\in W}$ with
priv$(2)=\{y_{2}\}$, priv$(3)=\{y_{3}\}$, priv$(8,9,10)=\{z_{1}\}$, priv$(1)=\{y_{1},z_{3}\}$.

EJR for $A_{6}$ needs $\max_{i\in A_{6}}|W\cap A_{i}|\ge 3$, so $w_{x}\ge 2$ is necessary.
The point is not the $2$-requirement for a $4$-subset, it is the interaction with the $3$-requirement for $A_{6}$ and the fact that all $4$-subsets share the same $3$-element core.

If $w_{x}=2$ the only way to reach $3$ for the $A_{6}$ group is to use a private seat. The private seats are disjoint across the sub-coalitions: $y_{2}$ helps only voter 2, $y_{3}$ only voter 3, $z_{1}$ only voters $8,9,10$, and $y_{1},z_{3}$ only voter 1. With only one seat left after the $w_{x}=2$ core and the two $Y$-seats forced by $B$, at most one of those private seats can be present.

Hence a consistent EJR committee must have the core elected: $w_{x}=3$. With $w_{x}=3$ we already have $|W\cap A_{i}|\ge3$ for voters $2,3,8,9,10$ on the $x$’s alone, and the $3$-cohesive $A_{6}$ is satisfied without using any private seat. So $|W\cap A_{1}|\ge w_{x}=3$ and $|W\cap A_{1}|=5-t\le3$. Thus
$|W\cap A_{1}|=3$.

The committee $W^{*}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$ shows the bound is attainable: $V_{1}=3$, $V_{2}=V_{3}=V_{8}=V_{9}=V_{10}=3$ on the $x$’s and $V_{4}=V_{5}=V_{6}=V_{7}=2$ on $y_{4},y_{5}$. No seat $y_{1}$ or $z_{3}$ can be added without losing a $Y$-seat and breaking $B$.

That is min $3$ max $3$ for voter 1, i.e. option E. The $w_{x}=2$ committees proposed as $W_{\min}$ use the private seat $z_{1}$ to give $3$ to voters $8\!-\!10$ while leaving voters $1,2,3$ with only $2$ $x$-approvals and they rely on the $2$-cohesive $\ell=2$ reading for the $4$-subsets. Under the nested core reading of Extended JR that is insufficient, and the $3$-element common intersection of every $4$-subset of $A_{6}$ forces $w_{x}=3$.
